## Traditional vs. Generative AI

| Aspect | Traditional AI (Analyzer) | Generative AI (Creator) |
|-------|----------------------------|-------------------------|
| Focus | Understand & Predict | Create & Generate |
| Output | Scores, forecasts, clusters | Drafts, briefs, scenarios |
| Data | Mostly structured | Mixed: text, code, images |
| UX | Dashboards | Conversations & agents |
| IR Use | Conflict prediction, voting patterns | Briefs, speeches, simulation scripts |

---

## Machine Learning: Learning from Data

```
📚 Data → 🔍 Patterns → 🧪 Predictions
        ↑                   ↓
        ← 🔄 Feedback ← ✨ Analysis
```

<div class="columns">
<div class="column">
  <div class="callout-note">
    <strong>Supervised:</strong> conflict prediction, election forecasting, sanctions effects
  </div>
</div>
<div class="column">
  <div class="callout-tip">
    <strong>Unsupervised:</strong> alliance clusters, UNGA voting blocs, narrative detection
  </div>
</div>
<div class="column">
  <div class="callout-important">
    <strong>Reinforcement:</strong> negotiation strategies, policy optimization, crisis games
  </div>
</div>
</div>

## Large Language Models (LLMs)

**Power**
- Global knowledge, multilingual
- Long-context reasoning (caveats)
- Flexible outputs (text, code, tables)
- Transfer & few-shot learning

**Leading families**
- GPT, Claude, Gemini
- Open models: Llama, Mixtral, DeepSeek

## Case Mini-Studies (Teaching Aids)

1) **Paris Agreement progress** – track pledges, narratives, and compliance signals.  
2) **Misinformation in crises** – detect coordinated narratives; propose counter-messaging.  
3) **Border incidents** – build a structured log; compare with historical de-escalation patterns.  
4) **UNGA voting blocs** – cluster countries; examine outliers and issue-specific coalitions.

<div class="prompt-box">
  <div class="prompt-title">💬 Try this Prompt</div>
  <div class="prompt-ex">"Cluster UNGA roll-call votes (provide a small sample) and explain which countries form stable coalitions across human-rights resolutions."</div>
</div>

---

## Building a Simple IR Workflow (RAG)

**Flow:** Sources → Chunk/Index → Retrieve → LLM → Cite → Human review  
- Start with open sources (UN, World Bank, think tanks)  
- Maintain a small, vetted corpus
- Use retrieval augmentation (RAG) for citations
- Document prompts & versions
- Keep a review checklist (facts, tone, bias, sensitivity)

<div class="prompt-box">
  <div class="prompt-title">💬 Try this Prompt</div>
  <div class="prompt-ex">"Given these 3 URLs (paste), build a 7-bullet brief with inline citations [1][2][3], flag contradictions, and list unknowns to investigate."</div>
</div>

---

## Human + AI: A Division of Labor

**AI excels at:** breadth, speed, synthesis, multilingual processing  
**Humans excel at:** judgment, context, ethics, accountability, diplomacy

<div class="gradient-box gradient-blue">
  <strong>Use AI for drafts; use humans for decisions.</strong>
</div>

---

## Risks, Limits, and Guardrails {.scrollable}

- **Bias** in training data → skewed outputs  
- **Hallucinations** → fabricated facts/citations  
- **Misinformation** → narrative amplification risks  
- **Privacy & security** → sensitive sources  
- **Over-reliance** → deskilling of analytic craft

<div class="callout-warning">
  Always verify with primary sources; keep an audit trail of prompts and revisions.
</div>

<div class="prompt-box">
  <div class="prompt-title">💬 Try this Prompt</div>
  <div class="prompt-ex">"List 5 potential harms of using AI to analyze conflict data and propose 5 mitigation steps a university lab can implement."</div>
</div>

---

## Ethics for IR & Academia

1. **Transparency** — disclose AI use when appropriate  
2. **Attribution** — credit sources & collaborators  
3. **Verification** — cross-check facts; log methods  
4. **Privacy** — protect vulnerable groups & data  
5. **Balance** — AI assists; humans decide

<div class="prompt-box">
  <div class="prompt-title">💬 Try this Prompt</div>
  <div class="prompt-ex">"Create a 1-page 'Responsible AI in the Seminar' policy for undergraduates with bullet points on disclosure, verification, and collaboration norms."</div>
</div>

---

## Teaching with AI: Faculty Notes

- Scaffold tasks (describe → compare → critique → create)  
- Encourage method transparency (prompt logs)  
- Evaluate process, not just outputs  
- Mix closed-book & oral checks to deter over-reliance  
- Bring country/regional expertise into AI prompts

---

## Skill Map: 6-Hour Path (for a mini-course)

- **Hour 1:** Concepts & vocabulary (this deck)  
- **Hour 2:** Prompt engineering for IR tasks  
- **Hour 3:** Research tools & RAG setup  
- **Hour 4:** Policy analysis & scenario design  
- **Hour 5:** Workflow automation & citing  
- **Hour 6:** Ethics lab & capstone presentations

---

## Quick Reference Prompts (Copy & Use)

- **Briefing:** “Summarize [topic] in 6 bullets for a minister, add 2 risks & 2 options.”  
- **Compare:** “Contrast positions of [A] vs [B] on [issue] with a 5-row table.”  
- **Narratives:** “Extract 3 narratives and their evidence from these links: [..].”  
- **Diplomatic style:** “Rewrite this memo in a neutral MFA tone, max 180 words.”  
- **Translation check:** “Translate to [lang] and back-translate; list divergences.”  
- **Scenario:** “Draft 3 scenarios (optimistic/base/pessimistic) with signposts.”
